passage.title: Reading passage (the 23.1 article, “Life in a Medieval Castle”)
passage.text:
A medieval castle was not just a home — it was a fortress, a workplace, and a whole community. The king or lord often lived in the strongest part of the castle, called the keep. Surrounding the keep were great halls, kitchens, stables, and chapels. Many people worked inside the castle walls every day.
Most castle workers were servants. Some cooked food, others cleaned, and some cared for the horses. Young boys from noble families could become pages, training to be knights one day. The castle was always busy — and always protected.
